claims.claim: Jeanie originated in 1977 inside Fifth Third's Midwest Payment Systems as the first shared online ATM network in the US.
claims.quote: In 1977, Jeanie, the nation's first shared online ATM network was developed and implemented.
claims.title: Worldpay, Inc. - Wikipedia (redirect from Jeanie (interbank network))
claims.label: Reported
claims.note: The Jeanie article redirects to the Worldpay, Inc. article; Jeanie has no standalone Wikipedia page.

claims.claim: Worldpay's ownership chain since 2019: FIS bought it in 2019, GTCR took 55% in 2023, it separated from FIS in 2024, and Global Payments completed its acquisition in 2026.
claims.quote: 2023: GTCR acquired 55% stake for $11.7 billion; 2024: Separated from FIS as independent company; 2026: Global Payments completed acquisition
claims.title: Worldpay, Inc. - Wikipedia
claims.label: Reported
claims.note: Quote is the timeline as summarised by the fetch tool from the article's history section; verified against the Global Payments 8-K below for the 2026 step.

claims.claim: Worldpay (and therefore Jeanie) is headquartered in Cincinnati, Ohio, with an international headquarters in London.
claims.quote: Based in Cincinnati, Ohio with international headquarters in London; operates 40 offices across 25 countries.
claims.title: Worldpay, Inc. - Wikipedia
claims.label: Reported

claims.claim: Global Payments completed its acquisition of Worldpay from FIS and GTCR on January 12, 2026, so Jeanie's ultimate owner is now Global Payments, not GTCR/FIS.
claims.quote: today announced the successful completion of its acquisition of Worldpay from FIS and GTCR, and the divestiture of its Issuer Solutions business to FIS.
claims.title: Exhibit 99.1 - Global Payments Completes Acquisition of Worldpay and Divestiture of Issuer Solutions Business (8-K, Global Payments Inc.)
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Dated 'ATLANTA - January 12, 2026 7:00am ET'. The press release does not name Jeanie or NYCE. This postdates and supersedes the task brief's description of Worldpay as GTCR-majority.

claims.claim: The Global Payments-Worldpay Transaction Agreement was signed on April 17, 2025, with closing on the date of the January 12, 2026 8-K.
claims.quote: on April 17, 2025, the Company, the Chicago Aggregator, Worldpay Holdco, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (“ Washington ”), and the other parties thereto, entered into a Transaction Agreement
claims.title: Exhibit 4.1 - Shareholders Agreement (8-K, Global Payments Inc., accession 0001104659-26-002705)
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Same exhibit: 'on the date hereof the Company directly or indirectly acquired 100% of the issued and outstanding equity interests of Washington'. Worldpay Holdco, LLC is the legal entity.

claims.claim: Global Payments filed an 8-K on January 12, 2026 under Items 1.01, 2.01, 3.02, 7.01 and 9.01 (completion of acquisition), followed by Item 5.02 8-Ks on January 14 and February 18, 2026.
claims.title: EDGAR filing index - Global Payments Inc. 8-K filings
claims.label: Verified

claims.claim: Post-close, the combined Global Payments/Worldpay serves more than 6 million merchant locations, $3.7 trillion in volume and about 94 billion transactions annually; no Jeanie-specific volume is published.
claims.quote: The combined company will serve more than 6 million merchant locations, processing $3.7 trillion in payment volume and approximately 94 billion transactions annually across more than 175 countries.
claims.title: Exhibit 99.1 - Global Payments Completes Acquisition of Worldpay
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Group-level figure, not a Jeanie network figure.

claims.claim: The Federal Reserve classifies Jeanie as a single-message (PIN) debit network in its Regulation II network-level interchange table, alongside ACCEL, AFFN, ATH, Culiance, Interlink, Maestro, NYCE, PULSE, SHAZAM and STAR.
claims.title: Federal Reserve Board - Regulation II - Average Debit Card Interchange Fee by Payment Card Network
claims.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Calendar-year 2024 data; page shows 'Last Update: December 19, 2025'. Ellipses mark omitted rows for other networks in the same table.

claims.claim: In calendar 2024 Jeanie's average interchange fee across all transactions was $0.17 per transaction, 0.79% of an average $21.22 transaction, per Fed Regulation II data.
claims.title: Federal Reserve Board - Regulation II - Average Debit Card Interchange Fee by Payment Card Network
claims.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Column order: exempt (% of count, % of value, avg value, avg fee, fee %), covered (same five), all (avg value, avg fee, fee %). Jeanie's covered-issuer average transaction value of $20.00 is far below every other listed network (e.g. NYCE $49.74, PULSE $48.31).

claims.claim: Jeanie's 2024 volume is overwhelmingly covered-issuer traffic: 98.3% of transactions and 92.7% of value came from issuers subject to the Reg II interchange cap.
claims.title: Federal Reserve Board - Regulation II - Average Debit Card Interchange Fee by Payment Card Network
claims.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Implies Jeanie's issuer base is dominated by large (covered) issuers, consistent with its Fifth Third heritage.

claims.claim: The Fed defines single-message networks (Jeanie's category) as those normally processing PIN-authenticated transactions with a single message to authorize and clear.
claims.quote: A payment card network that typically uses a single message to authorize and clear a transaction. These networks normally process PIN-authenticated transactions
claims.title: Federal Reserve Board - Regulation II - Average Debit Card Interchange Fee by Payment Card Network
claims.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
claims.label: Verified

claims.claim: The Fed's Regulation II data collections page lists the Payment Card Network survey instruments (through calendar 2024) and the combined 2023 report; it does not name Jeanie individually.
claims.quote: This survey solicits information regarding (1) volumes and values of debit card transactions...processed by the network; (2) interchange fees paid by acquirers and received by issuers.
claims.title: Federal Reserve Board - Regulation II - Data Collections
claims.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
